title: Reploid · Doppler · Doe
subtitle: Products that stand alone. Cooperation that earns its benefits.
basis: Revision of the supplied diagram using the user-provided product descriptions and review feedback. No repository audit, implementation certification, benchmark verification or product-roadmap verification is asserted.

entities.label: Reploid
entities.responsibility: Coordinate and improve distributed intelligence; Poolday connects participants and exchanges authorized data.
owns: Concurrent conversations and authorized agent workflows
Placement, budgets, Bayesian decision-making and recovery choices
Poolday: peer connectivity, bounded WebRTC delivery and authorized artifact/activation exchange
Mechanisms for independent strategy evaluation and reversible adoption
excludes: Model mathematics, learned expert selection and tensor semantics
WGSL compiler or native GPU runtime implementation
Automatic disclosure, compute contribution or code adoption merely from joining
Other projects’ evaluator, release or adoption authority
entities.independence: An agent may operate independently; the collaborating network remains the product.
entities.benefit: Collaborate through an intelligence network that pools participating devices’ capabilities.

entities.label: Doppler
entities.responsibility: Rig prepares and qualifies model implementations; Run executes the selected, identified implementation.
owns: Rig: source interpretation, ModelIR, TargetPlans, preparation and qualification
Capsules: identified executable implementations, weights and required dependencies
Run: resource loading, model operations, compatible adapters and valid computational partitions
Model mathematics, sampling, tensor interfaces and generation-state semantics
excludes: Peer membership, disclosure grants and network placement authority
Silent alteration of selected model semantics during ordinary execution
entities.independence: Usable without Reploid and with supported WebGPU providers other than Doe.
entities.benefit: Integrate and run model computation through a portable, straightforward interface.

entities.label: Doe
entities.responsibility: Compile WGSL and implement GPU execution while preserving declared application semantics.
owns: WGSL compilation and general shader optimization
Native Metal, Vulkan and D3D12 execution paths as qualified
Resources, synchronization, completion and observable failure behavior
General diagnostics and independently evaluated runtime/compiler corrections
excludes: Model selection, tokenization, quantization policy, search ranking or agent goals
Application-specific exceptions used to imply general superiority
Automatic replacement of the browser’s GPU implementation by a JavaScript import
entities.independence: Useful to applications unrelated to Doppler; integration requires an explicit provider boundary.
entities.benefit: Make supported existing GPU applications execute better without rewriting them.

applicationAdvantage.definition: At least one material application-valued improvement with predeclared limits on regressions in other relevant outcomes.
applicationAdvantage.validation: Compare unchanged applications on matched hardware, include independent non-Doppler applications, retain failures and scope claims to tested environments.

nonAssertions: Only Reploid–Doppler and Doppler–Doe are asserted symbiotic package relationships. No direct Reploid–Doe cooperation or dependency is implied.
Reciprocal evidence and mutual benefit are not reciprocal source dependencies.
Doppler can use other supported providers. Doe can serve independent applications and frameworks.
The diagrams describe intended contracts and workflows, not proven distributed execution, frontier-scale capability, beneficial recursive improvement or universal performance superiority.
Native provider integration and browser-engine integration are separate. Importing Doe does not replace the browser’s WebGPU implementation.
Storage sharding, whole-request execution, model partitioning and multi-agent task decomposition are distinct mechanisms.
Signed records identify accountable claims; they do not establish honest computation or scientific truth.
A success branch, a cancellation branch and a failure branch are alternatives during one attempt, not a sequence in which failure happens after successful completion.

edges.label: Qualify
details: The model implementation and its source-derived semantics have their own qualification. Changing them produces a new candidate and identity, not an in-place Run mutation.

edges.label: Evaluate
details: A Doppler release does not automatically approve adoption by Reploid. Test unfamiliar relevant work under the application’s own requirements.

edges.label: Application outcomes → strategy evaluation
details: Reploid may propose planning, context, tool or scheduling changes informed by authorized outcomes.
Evaluate strategy candidates separately; posterior updates, model changes and recursive improvement are different claims.

edges.label: Validate
details: Measure against a credible incumbent on matched hardware. Include applications unrelated to Doppler.
Do not automatically attribute every application gain to Doe or require every metric to improve.

edges.label: Release
details: The provider release is separately versioned. Doppler and other recipients independently decide whether to use it.

notes.label: Real problem → reproduce → correct owner → validate → release → benefit
notes.text: Corrections stay in their responsible layer. Feedback contains authorized evidence, not implicit access to private conversations.

notes.label: Loop A ↔ B · Reploid application and Doppler implementation
Loop B ↔ C · Doppler workloads and Doe execution
notes.text: Provider corrections stay in Doe; independent applications validate benefits; each consumer chooses adoption.

notes.label: Measure benefit and development efficiency
notes.text: Track reproduction-to-verified-improvement time, application outcomes, regressions and independent transfer. This loop is not a runtime gate.

notes.text: These are distinct states with different evidence and authority; never combine them into one “eligible” badge.

notes.label: Every request binds its contract
notes.text: Attempt and implementation/Capsule identity · operation · permitted inputs · resource limits · cancellation handle.

views.title: Stream
views.subtitle: Remote whole-request example. Provider is selected once: Doe OR an environment-supported alternative, never both by implication.

edges.label: Authorize and send exact request
details: A human or authorized agent submits a message in a particular thread.
Q first distinguishes advertised capability from authorized placement. R independently validates the request before Run invocation.

edges.label: Prepare resources and programs
details: The selected provider is Doe only if its integration is supported on this host. Otherwise use the environment’s other supported provider.
Preparation failures branch to recovery; they do not imply proceeding through successful streaming.

edges.label: Bound event → same message
details: Accept only the active attempt and compatible event ordering. Ignore or quarantine late output from a superseded attempt.
Cancellation or failure branches can occur during this loop, not only after it finishes.

edges.label: Final output + execution identity
edges.guard: Complete computation and valid terminal event

edges.label: Completion → requester acceptance
details: Only the success branch terminates as an accepted complete answer.
Cancellation and recovery are alternate paths starting during execution, not subsequent success steps.
edges.guard: Requester checks the bound identity, event chain and declared acceptance conditions

notes.label: Execution host contains the receiver, Run and one selected provider
Alternative outcomes: success OR cancellation OR failure
notes.text: Local placement bypasses Poolday transport. Open Cancel or Recover for branches from the active stream; neither follows a successful answer.

bands.label: LOOP · repeat bounded computation and ordered output; cancellation or failure may branch at any iteration
SUCCESS BRANCH ONLY · final output must meet the requester’s acceptance contract

fragments.guard: No terminal outcome, grants remain valid and budgets permit execution

views.title: Cancel
views.subtitle: A cancellation branch during streaming. Acknowledging the request, stopping output and settling owned work are different events.

edges.label: Requester asks to stop attempt
details: Initiated by the human/agent controlling the thread. Q suppresses further display for this cancelled attempt while remote settlement remains pending.

edges.label: Participant stops contributed work
details: Alternative initiation: the execution-device operator or its resource policy stops this attempt. It need not wait for a requester command.

edges.label: Settle this attempt’s submitted work
details: Use the provider’s supported completion and resource-lifetime contract. Do not depict this as guaranteed GPU preemption.
Do not destroy a shared GPU device or release another thread’s resources.

edges.label: Output stopped; settlement pending
details: This acknowledgement says no more output will be forwarded for the attempt. It does not prove submitted GPU work has finished.

edges.label: Cleanup confirmed for this attempt
details: Only this confirmation establishes known remote settlement. Loss of the peer or acknowledgement leaves the requester’s cleanup knowledge unknown.
edges.guard: Confirmation delivered and bound to the same attempt

notes.label: Execution peer retains responsibility for its own resources
If the peer disappears: cleanup unknown, not cleanup confirmed
notes.text: Keep this attempt’s late output out of replacement attempts. Cancelling one thread must not stop unrelated threads.

bands.label: ALT INITIATOR A · requester cancels during normal execution
ALT INITIATOR B · execution participant or its policy cancels; not a second mandatory command
COMMON CANCELLATION PATH · acknowledgements do not promise immediate GPU termination
SETTLEMENT · only after owned work and state have actually settled

views.title: Recover
views.subtitle: Failure branch from an active attempt. Local observation of a lost peer is not an acknowledgement of remote cleanup.

Are plan, state, recipients and limits valid?
Resume, start a new attempt, or stay stopped

and observed cleanup status

Cleanup UNKNOWN

notes.text: Doppler → other supported WebGPU providers. Other applications/frameworks → Doe. Neither product is captive to the other.

compatibility.extensionPolicy: Extra semantic fields describe contracts, guards and cross-view relationships. All essential visible content also uses existing v1 nodes, edges, notes or bands; no new drawing primitive is required.
compatibility.coordinatePolicy: Absolute diagram coordinates, x right and y down. Sequence messages are horizontal; graph edges use explicit anchors and waypoints.

claimPolicy.milestones: planned; require evidence before a capability claim
claimPolicy.performance: A material application advantage under predeclared regression limits, not simultaneous improvement in every metric.
claimPolicy.independence: Separate evaluation, release and adoption authority. Runtime activity under valid grants is not gated by the development-time improvement loop.

contributions.provides: Authorized application workloads, demand, environment observations and reproducible failures
Portable model execution, valid computational contracts and newly qualified implementations
Reproducible shader workloads, complete application comparisons and developer access
General compiler/runtime corrections and a qualified optional execution provider

reploid-doppler.status: proposed contract description; labels are not assertions of exported API names
reploid-doppler.callee: Doppler Run on the execution host
fields: cancellation handle scoped to this attempt
reploid-doppler.authority: Reploid places eligible work; Doppler defines and executes valid model computation. Ordinary Run does not silently reprepare or modify the selected implementation.

peer-request.transport: Poolday WebRTC after authorized receiving-interface validation

decisions.meaning: A participant claims a capability; no grant or execution acceptance follows.
Placement matches verified contracts, participant membership, disclosure grants, budgets and freshness.
The returned execution satisfies the requester’s declared acceptance conditions; this is not a truth guarantee.

peer-request.localBypass: A local request calls local receiving/execution interfaces directly. No WebRTC transmission is required; applicable permission and identity checks still apply.

doppler-provider.selectedBy: Execution host / environment through an explicit supported provider integration
doppler-provider.selection: Exactly one compatible provider for the illustrated execution context; the unselected branch emits no responses.
doppler-provider.ownership: Doppler owns model semantics. The provider owns shader compilation and GPU execution.
doppler-provider.browserBoundary: Use the browser’s exposed implementation unless a separately integrated browser engine supplies Doe. A package import does not replace it.

rules: Bind output to the active attempt, not just the thread.
Sequence events and reject incompatible duplicates or gaps under the chosen delivery contract.
Ignore or quarantine late events from a superseded attempt.
Do not combine a restarted generation with the old partial answer.
Acknowledging a request is not confirmation of resource settlement.
Stop new dispatch and result forwarding for this attempt.
Wait for submitted or borrowed GPU work according to the execution contract.
Do not destroy a shared device or cancel unrelated threads.
If the execution peer disappears before confirmation, report cleanup unknown.

dopplerAssesses: token position and relevant generation-state ownership
rules: Recheck grants and budgets before recovery.
A replacement attempt gets a new attemptId and a separate output stream.
A journal or receipt alone cannot reconstruct lost GPU state.
Continuation is allowed only through Doppler’s declared contract; otherwise restart or stop.

improvement-evidence.privacy: No automatic export of private conversations, documents, activations or credentials. Redact or replace inputs only when the resulting reproduction remains valid and authorized.
improvement-evidence.attribution: Fix the responsible layer; preserve independent evaluator, release and adopter authority.
metrics: time from accepted reproduction to independently verified improvement
improvement-evidence.comparison: Freeze application semantics, workload, measurement scope and budgets. A semantic/model change becomes a separately identified qualified implementation; a provider comparison keeps the application unchanged.

choices.guard: Supported and explicitly integrated on this execution host

branches.guard: Complete output accepted under the bound contract
Execution error, invalid state, deadline failure or lost peer
